storyboard.claim: Scrolling keeps the brain working hard, so the screen break is not rest.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A woman with a phone, brow furrowed, deep in thought.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the screen-break argument from the feed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strain is shown as the furrowed brow; the phone is a held object, not an icon.

storyboard.claim: The brain was never rested; only the app changed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman slumped, still tired, with no rest visible.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the feed scene: the machine is still running.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout carries the software metaphor; the slump shows no recovery.

storyboard.claim: Real recovery needs a physical state change.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman speaking to camera, explaining the idea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the problem to the fix.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the fix as a body change rather than a screen change.

storyboard.claim: Recovery means leaving the desk and moving the body.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman walking away from a desk toward a window of daylight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the concrete actions behind the state change.
storyboard.addedInformation: The walk makes the step-away literal; the daylight stands for outdoor light.

storyboard.claim: Drinking water rehydrates the brain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lightbulb glowing over a woman holding a cup of water, the brain rehydrating.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First of the physical resets named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Water icon reads literally as water to drink.

storyboard.claim: Breath of fire is a forceful breathing exercise.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman explaining the breath technique.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the breathing technique from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout names the exhalation pattern; no icon fits a breathing exercise literally.

storyboard.claim: Breath of fire wakes the brain more than caffeine.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman raising a cup in a celebratory gesture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Compares the breath to a familiar stimulant.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cup carries the espresso comparison without being a metaphor for money or time.

storyboard.claim: A short walk resets the brain chemistry.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman walking around a block.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the physical reset in one concrete action.
storyboard.addedInformation: The walk makes the 5-minute duration concrete.

storyboard.claim: Changing screens drains the brain; it does not recharge it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A phone icon with the woman slumped beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the phone break from the opening.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone icon reads as the modern smartphone the narration means.

storyboard.claim: Recovery is a decision, not a calendar entry.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman standing at a desk, deciding whether to walk away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the recovery segment with the book's decision framing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Staging shows a choice being weighed rather than a schedule being set.

storyboard.claim: Mastering the tools still leaves a deeper problem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman thinking through a long list of tools.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from the recovery tactics to the acceptance problem.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout introduces the turn; the thinking pose carries the doubt.

storyboard.claim: Ambition eventually meets a limit that cannot be argued away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman sitting still, sad, facing the limit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the acceptance scenario.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sad face with idle pose: the emotion carries the acceptance, no icon needed.

storyboard.claim: A student faces an impossible night of study at midnight.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A woman at a library table at night, a stack of study notes in front of her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the student scenario.
storyboard.addedInformation: Library set and book icon read as study at night.

storyboard.claim: The exam deadline is hours away and the reading is not done.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock icon beside the woman, afraid, at the library table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the deadline to the student scenario.
storyboard.addedInformation: Clock icon reads as a deadline here, which is literal to the exam time.

storyboard.claim: The reading cannot all fit into the hours left.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman slumped at the library table, defeated.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the deadline is impossible.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump shows the realisation; the callout states the arithmetic verdict.

storyboard.claim: Letting go is the final lesson from Cruz's research.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz, sad and thoughtful, reflecting on the lesson.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ties the student scenario back to Cruz's research.
storyboard.addedInformation: Cruz is on screen because the narration names his research as the source.

storyboard.claim: Andy Grove described the same endless workload.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator voice over an empty frame; no visual claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces a named source for the endless-work argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Narrator is off-screen; the callout names the source.

storyboard.claim: A manager's workday never ends because the work never ends.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman thinking about an endless stack of papers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives Grove's point in the narrator's words.
storyboard.addedInformation: The thinking pose carries the endlessness; the callout states the claim.

storyboard.claim: The workday ends at exhaustion, not at completion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman slumped with her papers, exhausted.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the endless-work point with the exhaustion end.
storyboard.addedInformation: Slump plus sad shows exhaustion, the cost of never finishing.

storyboard.claim: Effort has no limit; time does.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman explaining that effort can always grow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the contrast with time in the next beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout states the claim; the talk pose keeps it explanatory.

storyboard.claim: Time is finite, unlike effort.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass beside the woman thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts with the effort point in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Hourglass reads as time running out, the literal meaning of finite time.

storyboard.claim: Maximum productivity comes from minimal effort on the right task.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman pointing at a single target-like choice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the principle the narration introduces.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pointing shows the choice of where to act.

storyboard.claim: Overdelivering on a task wastes your own time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman speaking, surprised at the claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the moral framing of overdelivering.
storyboard.addedInformation: Surprised face reflects the reversal of the usual praise for extra effort.

storyboard.claim: Overdoing one task steals hours from another.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow from overdoing A to stealing hours to underdoing B.
storyboard.onScreenText: Task A gets too much / You steal the hours / The work for B waits
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the cost of overdelivery as a chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: The flow makes the trade-off structural, not just stated.

storyboard.claim: The Pareto principle is the rule to apply everywhere.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman pointing at the choice of where to focus.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the flow with the solution.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pointing shows choosing where to put effort.

storyboard.claim: Stop once the 20 percent of effort is done.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman relaxed, having stopped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the 80/20 instruction.
storyboard.addedInformation: Relaxed idle pose makes the stop feel like permission.

storyboard.claim: Settling for good enough is hard advice for ambitious people.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman thinking hard about the advice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises the objection the host feels.
storyboard.addedInformation: Thinking pose shows the struggle with the idea.

storyboard.claim: The objection: ambition should aim for perfection.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman questioning, surprised, speaking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the objection in the listener's voice.
storyboard.addedInformation: Surprised and talking reads as questioning the advice.

storyboard.claim: The host rejects the framing that good enough is giving up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman speaking with a firm, disagreeing pose.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the objection from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the rejected framing; angry reads as disagreement.

callout.text: Aim for strategic excellence, not mediocrity

storyboard.claim: Strategic excellence, not perfectionism, avoids mediocrity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman explaining the counter-argument.
storyboard.onScreenText: Aim for strategic excellence, not mediocrity
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reverses the objection with the book's term.
storyboard.addedInformation: Happy talk reads as an explanation, not a threat.

storyboard.claim: Demanding perfection across all tasks spreads energy too thin.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman thinking, weighed down by a list of many tasks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the example of spreading perfectionism too far.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sad thinking shows the weight of the list.

storyboard.claim: Spreading effort thin makes you average at everything.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman slumped, worn out by too many tasks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the consequence of the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Slump shows the cost of spreading energy thin.

storyboard.claim: The 80/20 rule is a tool against guilt, not a license to be lazy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon beside the woman holding the idea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the rule as a psychological tool.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shield reads as protection against guilt; strike rejects the lazy reading.

storyboard.claim: Do the top 20 percent of work exceptionally well.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target icon beside the woman pointing at it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the rule as focus on the top priority.
storyboard.addedInformation: Target reads as aiming at the top-priority goal.

storyboard.claim: Consciously let the rest go.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman thinking calmly about what to drop.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what happens to the other tasks.
storyboard.addedInformation: Neutral thinking keeps the callout as the only voice on the letting-go.

storyboard.claim: Strategic excellence accepts a C minus on admin work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman pointing at a low-priority list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the concrete grade for low-priority work.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pointing marks which tasks to drop.

storyboard.claim: Being intentionally bad at unimportant things frees capacity for what matters.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman with a knowing smirk, talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the strategic choice.
storyboard.addedInformation: Smirk gives the intentional-badness claim an edge of wry charm.

storyboard.claim: Choosing your quality bar is a decision, not a scheduling task.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman thinking about where to set her bar.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the perfection argument with the decision frame.
storyboard.addedInformation: Thinking pose matches a decision being made.

storyboard.claim: The host now pauses to critique the whole framework.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman stopped, looking uneasy, pausing the argument.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the advice to a critique of it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Stopped pose reads as a pause before the critique.

storyboard.claim: Elite time management literature has a structural blind spot.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator voice over an empty frame; no visual claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the critique the next beats develop.
storyboard.addedInformation: Narrator is off-screen; the callout names the blind spot.
